key_insight: DATPO improves RLVR by making training rollouts difficulty-adaptive and tree-structured, which increases semantic exploration and expands pass@k rather than only boosting single-sample accuracy.
engineering_relevance: For reasoning-system builders, the paper suggests that better train-time exploration design can materially improve test-time scaling and multi-sample reliability on math tasks.
method: Difficulty-adaptive tree search chooses rollout structure based on problem difficulty.
Sentence-entropy-guided forking creates semantically diverse branches instead of token-level branching.
A sibling-diversity advantage term explicitly rewards diverse reasoning paths during policy optimization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on mathematical reasoning benchmarks, where DATPO outperforms baselines especially in pass@k, leading to better test-time scaling performance.
watch_item: Tree-structured, entropy-guided rollout design may add training complexity and tuning sensitivity, so gains could depend on careful implementation of branching and diversity signals.
paper_title: Difficulty-Adaptive Tree-Structured Policy Optimization for Expanding Reasoning Coverage in RLVR
